page: The UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-16GB is a starter-class virtual server configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Built on the KVM hypervisor, it utilizes x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processors running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the hardware features 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. Storage is bundled with a local 50 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core execution. However, due to its shared CPU allocation and low core count, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks fall into the weak category. This includes Geekbench multi-core, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 404.78 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 46.3 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU resource model, which limits sustained multi-threaded throughput and database operations, as evidenced by weak Passmark database and Redis SET performance. Qualitatively, the server offers high memory density at a starter-tier cost profile, making it cost-efficient for memory-heavy but compute-light workloads. It is best suited for lightweight background utilities, single-threaded text processing, small-scale LLM inference using small models, and basic memory-intensive caching that does not require sustained multi-core processing.
